results.claim: THEORY.md, R1: adaptive separation for Gaussian mass of unknown ellipsoids

human: Gilbert, Kuo and Sloan (2022), Theorem 1 on tangencies in linear preintegration
Plaskota and Wasilkowski (2005), adaptive/nonadaptive rates for one unknown singularity
comparison.explanation: Works for a narrower algebraic class, but handles intrinsically nonmonotone closed surfaces using value queries, gives a relative deterministic guarantee even at small Gaussian mass, and separates adaptive from arbitrary nonadaptive rules including randomized designs.

results.claim: THEORY.md, R2: antipodal recovery in the presence of an unknown odd background

human: Gilbert, Kuo and Sloan (2022), Theorem 1 on tangencies in linear preintegration
Plaskota and Wasilkowski (2005), one unknown singularity
comparison.explanation: Pairs of real values remove an infinite-dimensional nuisance exactly. The unknown offsets are recovered stably up to reflection, giving the same exponential precision order and nonadaptive obstruction for this restricted multidimensional class.

results.claim: THEORY.md, R3: exact background oracle reduction and decoding shell bound

human: Gilbert, Kuo and Sloan (2022), Theorem 1 on tangencies in linear preintegration
Plaskota and Wasilkowski (2005), one unknown singularity
Griewank, Kuo, Leövey and Sloan (2018), smoothness under strictly monotone preintegration
comparison.explanation: No globally monotone direction or oracle for the defining function is needed. The theorem restores an exact unrestricted-background query transcript with logarithmic-in-accuracy geometric cost and proves a relative shell bound for the extra calls. The boundary is restricted to well-scaled ellipsoids and the jump has known unit size, so this does not imply the human theorems on their broader geometric classes.

results.claim: THEORY.md, R4: exact dimension-dependent query threshold for continuous centered quadratic kinks

human: Bakhvalov (1959), optimal asymptotic query rates on smoothness classes
Plaskota and Wasilkowski (2005), adaptive localization of one unknown univariate singularity
comparison.explanation: A finite-parameter class permits exact cubature but requires the full quadratic parameter count below a positive error threshold, even with adaptive real queries. Neither standard smoothness rates nor results for one-dimensional singularities give this multivariate information threshold.

results.claim: THEORY.md, R5: adaptive exact recovery and integration in linear dimension for rank at most two

human: Liu and Owen (2023), active-subspace preintegration and scrambled-net variance comparison
Xiao and Wang (2019), gradient principal components for derivative pricing
comparison.explanation: The exact PSD rank restriction and pure cap form are stronger structural assumptions. Within them, a value-only rule uses at most 3d calls to recover the quadratic and the Gaussian integral, with a lower bound of d calls below a dimension-independent absolute tolerance. This addresses query complexity of unknown directions rather than variance after an active direction is provided.

results.claim: THEORY.md, R6: exact rank-adaptive cubature with no supplied rank or orientation

human: Liu and Owen (2023), active-subspace preintegration and scrambled-net variance comparison
Classical pivoted Cholesky on an available matrix
comparison.explanation: The rank and active range are inferred from the real payoff alone. In the pure PSD cap class the exact cost is bounded by d times (rank plus one) along the actual transcript, without specifying a rank bound in the algorithm. The class and zero-noise information model are narrower than the active-subspace and derivative-pricing models; the elimination identity itself is the classical Gram projection.

results.claim: THEORY.md, R7: stable linear-dimension reconstruction and Gaussian cubature for rank-two binary jumps

human: Gilbert, Kuo and Sloan (2022), Theorem 1 on tangencies in linear preintegration
Liu and Owen (2023), preintegration via an active subspace
comparison.explanation: A supplied witness of one curved ray is weaker information than an active basis or point access to the defining quadratic. The theorem recovers a rank-two centered jump from binary values with explicit linear dimension query count, uniform entry stability even near a rank change, and a deterministic Gaussian mass bound. It does not give preintegrand regularity or apply to general nonquadratic boundaries.
